theater.sub: The options the US has right now in the Iran war, and what followed the last times the US did something like each one.
theater.proxy_note: An Iran-backed group is a militia Iran arms in Iraq or Syria. Before 2026, Iran mostly answered the US through these groups; those replies count.
theater.hold_note: Hold cases are weeks of the 2026 war with no logged US sanctions, naval, strike or posture move (Feb 28-Apr 7 and Jul 7-25 left out: US activity there was continuous but logged as a few rows; pre-war weeks left out: too sparsely logged). Most hold weeks have few or no logged events, so they show what the log records in quiet weeks.
theater.not_measured: Oil prices, strain with allies and harm to ordinary Iranians are not measured.
theater.under_logged: The log is a sample. It starts at the Nov 1979 embassy takeover, but 1981-86, 1988-94, 1997-2001, 2003-05 and 2008-09 are thinly logged: before 2019 it holds the big crises, sanctions rounds, UN votes and talks, not every incident, and the Tanker War is logged as a few key clashes. Many pre-1990 rows rest on Washington Post archive pages. Some stretches are logged as one row (for example the nightly US strikes of Jul 9-25, 2026), so "none logged" is not proof nothing happened.

risks: Ship crews: attacks on shipping continue at ~2.4 a week (e.g. On Peace, Oct 6: 12 crew injured). No new US act to answer.
No new US trigger. Iranian or unidentified attacks on shipping keep happening anyway (baseline). Whether holding back changes Iran's behaviour: not measured.

Baseline: ~2.4 attacks on shipping a week in the current phase. Oil prices and shipping costs: not measured.
Iran is expected to answer the US counter-offer; Trump's no-strike pledge stands until Nov 3. Strain with allies: not measured.
options.pros: No new US act for Iran to answer, so no added risk of retaliation from it. Keeps Trump's stated no-strike pledge before Nov 3. Leaves room for Iran's expected reply to the US counter-offer. Uses no interceptors.
options.harms: Attacks on shipping continue at about 1-2 a week (baseline), injuring crews (On Peace: 12 hurt) and raising shipping risk. Whether holding back weakens deterrence cannot be measured from this log.
options.unknown: Shipping attacks have kept coming without any new US move (see the baseline line). Trump has said there will be no US strikes before Nov 3; what Iran does if that holds is not in the data.

forecasts.question: Will Iran hit back for the US strike that disabled a blockade runner in the Gulf of Oman (Oct 10-11, event #104)?
forecasts.note: NO. No allowed outlet or official statement reports an Iranian (IRGC or state) strike or attack on US forces, a US base, or a US-flagged or US-escorted ship during Oct 11-16. Al Jazeera (Oct 17) lists the week's attacks as all on commercial ships and says the US had not responded to them. Close call to note: Iran's security chief said (Oct 11) Iran was striking ships in the 'US-backed' oil shuttle, and the IRGC said one tanker hit on Oct 17-18 was crossing 'with US support'; no outlet says any ship hit Oct 11-16 was US-flagged or under US warship escort, and the Oct 17-18 claim falls after the deadline. CENTCOM's Oct 14 statement about a dhow 'targeting' US ships refers to Oct 6 surveillance, before the window.
forecasts.basis: Phase model (best in backtest): in the current holding pattern 0 of 2 hostile acts drew a reply -> (0+1)/(2+2) = 25%. For comparison, naval-pressure moves in ALL phases drew a reply 2 of 3 (67%). Also: Trump says no US strikes before Nov 3; Iran is reviewing the US counter-offer.

forecasts.question: Will there be at least one new attack on a commercial ship in or near the Strait of Hormuz / Gulf (by Iran or an unidentified attacker) during Oct 12-18?
forecasts.note: YES. On Oct 13 the Singapore-flagged container ship GFS Pride was hit by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz and sank (Reuters, citing Singapore's MPA; all 21 crew safe), and UKMTO reported a tanker hit the same day (Al Jazeera). CENTCOM said an IRGC projectile hit GFS Pride. More attacks followed (Oct 16-17 off Saudi Arabia; UKMTO counted 10-12 in the week to Oct 16).
forecasts.basis: Baseline: 8 such acts in 4.6 weeks of the current phase = 1.8 per week. Chance of at least one in a week (Poisson) = 1 - e^-1.8 = 83%.

forecasts.question: Will the US strike a target on Iranian land or in Iranian territorial waters between Oct 20 and Nov 3 (inclusive)?
forecasts.basis: Phase base rate: in the holding pattern (since Sep 10) there have been 0 US strikes on Iranian land in 5 full weeks -> weekly chance (0+1)/(5+2) = 14%; over 15 days 1-(1-0.14)^(15/7) = 28%. Not in the model: Trump's public pledge of no strikes before Nov 3 (#97) and reported strike plans (#111).

forecasts.question: Will there be at least one new attack on a commercial ship in or near the Strait of Hormuz / Gulf (by Iran or an unidentified attacker) during Oct 19-25?
